This repo uses a **three-layer Markdown-driven knowledge architecture**:

1. **Auto-applied instructions** (`.github/instructions/`) — Feature-scoped constraints and rules
2. **Behavioral context documents** (`<module>/docs/<area>/<feature>/`) — Pre-built architectural knowledge

1. Check `.github/ai-knowledge-registry.yml` for available feature areas
2. Read the `INDEX.md` file for your feature (e.g., `core/printegrint/docs/security/scim/INDEX.md`)
3. Follow the routing table in INDEX.md to load relevant context documents
4. Apply the feature-specific `.instructions.md` rules

- ❌ **NEVER** hardcode passwords, API keys, tokens, or secrets in any file

- ✅ **All** code changes MUST be backward compatible

- ✅ **Propose** code with exact file paths and method locations

When working with SCIM identity provisioning files:

1. Read `.github/instructions/security-scim.instructions.md`

- Provide **diffs or search/replace blocks** — NOT entire files

- **Update** `ARCHITECTURE-OVERVIEW.md` for structural changes
- **Update** production readiness checklist when changing tests

- `.github/instructions/*.instructions.md`

- **Instruction conflicts**: Multiple instruction files covering the same source files
- **Broken references**: Links in docs that point to non-existent files
- **Ownership tagging**: Automatic owner notification via CODEOWNERS rules

To acknowledge findings without fixing immediately, add to your PR description:

44	### Definitions & Scope
45	
46	- **Affected user**: the single mapped operator identity (one tenant-scoped identity) for whom a trigger event establishes or advances an invalidation boundary. No other operator or tenant is in scope of that event.
47	- **User-facing local password change**: a user-facing operation in which the affected operator changes their own existing effective local password only through (a) the authenticated standard self-service change-password flow or (b) the user-facing forgot-password/account-recovery flow after the existing proof/OTP validation establishes control of that same account. Scope is determined by flow origin plus actor/subject ownership, not role: an operator with administrator privileges is included when changing their own password through either included user-facing flow. Administrator password management of another operator — changing, setting, resetting, unlocking-and-generating, or otherwise managing that operator's password through an administrative UI, activity, API, bulk operation, or generic operator save — MUST NOT establish or advance this feature's invalidation boundary and MUST NOT create a trigger or audit lifecycle; existing behavior outside this feature remains unchanged. First-time password sets, failed, rolled-back, no-op, and maintenance-only changes are excluded.
48	- **Invalidation boundary**: a point in time, tracked per affected user, after which every item of pre-boundary covered access for that user is treated as no longer valid. The boundary only ever advances; it never moves backward.
49	- **Pre-boundary access**: any covered access item (see inventory below) that was issued or established before the affected user's current invalidation boundary.
50	- **Post-boundary access**: any covered access item established by a fresh, successful authentication that occurs after the invalidation boundary and is evaluated under current identity authority and policy.
51	- **Covered Pega-managed access inventory**: the complete, fixed set of access items subject to invalidation for the affected user — active and stored-inactive browser sessions; active and stored-inactive service sessions; programmatic and mobile access; Pega application authentication tokens; Pega-issued user access credentials; and Pega-issued refresh credentials — on every cluster node, regardless of which authentication path (Basic, or a configured identity provider) originally established each item.
52	- **Covered-access invalidation outcome (user-facing behavior)**: the single normalized outcome produced on the next use of any invalidated covered access item: the item is treated exactly like an expired or terminated session and is presented through the platform's existing session-expiry/termination experience (existing re-authentication prompt/redirect); no new user-facing message or flow is introduced.
53	- **Final permission check immediately before protected work begins** (business authorization boundary): the last point, for any unit of protected work, at which current identity authority and the invalidation boundary are evaluated before that unit of work is allowed to start doing anything irreversible. 54	- **Trigger outcome**: because a local password change is a single, synchronous, user-initiated operation (not a redeliverable external event), each trigger produces exactly one of two outcomes: **Completed** (the change committed and the invalidation boundary is enforceable — this is also the point at which the change is reported successful to the user) or **Not completed** (the change did not commit, or committed but the boundary could not be made enforceable — reported to the user as "not completed; retry required", never as success).

120	### Edge Cases
121	
122	- What happens when protected work started before the invalidation boundary has not yet passed its final permission check by the time invalidation is enforced? It must fail and require fresh authentication; it is not allowed to complete using stale authority.

124	- What happens if the invalidation boundary cannot be made enforceable at commit time? 125	- What happens to unaffected operators during any invalidation event or any status-unavailable condition? They see no impact whatsoever.
126	- What happens when a new, valid authentication attempt occurs after the boundary is set? It is evaluated under current identity authority and policy and may succeed, establishing new valid post-boundary access.
127	- What happens on a node restart, or if the cluster broadcast of a boundary is delayed or missed by a node? That node still enforces the boundary correctly on next access, because enforcement is derived from an existing persisted signal, not from having received the broadcast (see FR-010).
